stem: An auditor asks a company for AWS's SOC 2 report and its PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance.
prompt: Where can the company download these documents?

options.why: Config tracks your resource configurations.
Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and agreements.
Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, not audit reports.

explanation.answer: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for AWS compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) and agreements such as the BAA.
explanation.concept: These reports show how AWS meets its side of the shared responsibility model.
explanation.examTip: AWS's audit reports and agreements = AWS Artifact.

stem: A healthcare company in the United States must sign a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) with AWS before storing protected health information.
prompt: How can it review and accept the BAA?

options.why: Marketplace sells third-party software, not AWS agreements.
Macie finds sensitive data, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
AWS Artifact lets customers review, accept and manage agreements such as the BAA.
SCPs limit permissions; they don't manage agreements.

explanation.answer: AWS Artifact Agreements lets you review, accept and track agreements like the Business Associate Addendum for HIPAA.
explanation.concept: You can accept agreements for a single account or for all accounts in an organization.
explanation.examTip: BAA for HIPAA = AWS Artifact Agreements.

stem: A company must continuously collect evidence from its AWS usage to prepare for audits against frameworks such as SOC 2 and GDPR.
prompt: Which service automates this evidence collection?

options.why: Cost Explorer analyzes spending, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Artifact provides AWS's own reports, not evidence about your usage.
Trusted Advisor gives recommendations, not audit evidence.
Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from your AWS usage mapped to compliance frameworks.

explanation.answer: AWS Audit Manager automates evidence collection to help you assess whether your policies, procedures and activities are operating effectively.
explanation.concept: Artifact = AWS's compliance. Audit Manager = your compliance evidence.
explanation.examTip: Collect audit evidence about your own usage = Audit Manager.

stem: A company must show auditors that all its EBS volumes have been encrypted continuously over the last six months.
prompt: Which service records configuration history and compliance with rules?

options.why: Config records configuration changes and evaluates compliance with rules over time.
Trusted Advisor gives point-in-time checks, not configuration history against rules.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
CloudTrail records who made API calls, but Config records configuration history and rule compliance.

explanation.answer: AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and evaluates them against rules, providing a compliance timeline.
explanation.concept: Config conformance packs bundle rules for common frameworks.
explanation.examTip: Configuration history and compliance over time = AWS Config.

stem: A security team wants to know which IAM user deleted an S3 bucket yesterday.

options.why: Metrics measure performance, not who made API calls.
CloudTrail records API calls with the identity, time and source.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Config shows the configuration change but CloudTrail records who made the call.

explanation.answer: AWS CloudTrail records actions taken by users, roles and services as events, including who did what, when and from where.
explanation.concept: CloudTrail event history shows the past 90 days of management events by default.
explanation.examTip: Who did what, when = CloudTrail.

stem: A team is confused about Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail.

options.text: CloudWatch records API calls; CloudTrail monitors CPU usage
options.why: These are reversed, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: Both services only store billing data
options.why: Neither is mainly a billing service, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

options.text: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs; CloudTrail records API activity
options.why: CloudWatch is for performance monitoring and alarms; CloudTrail is for auditing actions.

options.text: They are the same service with two names
options.why: They're different services with different purposes.

explanation.answer: Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics, logs and events and sets alarms. AWS CloudTrail logs API calls for governance and auditing.
explanation.concept: Use both together: CloudWatch for "how is it running?" and CloudTrail for "who changed it?"
explanation.examTip: CloudWatch = performance. CloudTrail = audit trail of API calls.

stem: A payment company asks whether AWS infrastructure is assessed against PCI DSS.
prompt: Where can it find which services are in scope for PCI DSS?

options.text: The AWS Artifact agreements page only
options.why: Artifact provides reports and agreements; the in-scope list is on the compliance website.

options.text: The AWS Billing console under each service
options.why: Billing shows charges, not compliance scope.
Trusted Advisor doesn't list compliance scope.

options.text: The AWS Services in Scope by Compliance page
options.why: This page lists services covered by each compliance program.

explanation.answer: AWS publishes which services are in scope for each compliance program, such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC and ISO.
explanation.concept: Using in-scope services is necessary but not enough; customers must also configure them correctly.
explanation.examTip: Is this service in scope for PCI/HIPAA? = AWS Services in Scope page.

references.title: AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program

stem: A company runs its workload only on AWS services that are in scope for HIPAA.
prompt: Is the workload automatically HIPAA compliant?

options.text: No; it must still configure and operate it correctly
options.why: Compliance is shared: AWS covers the infrastructure, and the customer covers its configuration and processes.

options.text: Yes, as long as it has Enterprise Support
options.why: Support plans don't make workloads compliant.

options.text: Yes; in-scope services make the workload compliant
options.why: Using in-scope services is necessary but not sufficient.

options.text: No; HIPAA workloads can't run on AWS
options.why: Many HIPAA workloads run on AWS under a BAA.

explanation.answer: Compliance is a shared responsibility. AWS provides compliant infrastructure; customers must secure and configure their applications and data.
explanation.concept: Use AWS Artifact, AWS Config and AWS Audit Manager to support your compliance program.
explanation.examTip: In-scope service ≠ automatically compliant workload.

stem: A company must keep a record of all API activity in its account for seven years.

options.text: An AWS Config rule for each API action
options.why: Config evaluates resource configurations; it doesn't store API activity logs.

options.text: A CloudTrail trail delivering logs to Amazon S3
options.why: A trail stores events in S3, where they can be retained as long as needed.

options.text: CloudWatch alarms on API call counts
options.why: Alarms notify; they don't keep a record of every API call.

options.text: Rely on CloudTrail event history in the console
options.why: Event history keeps only 90 days, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: A CloudTrail trail delivers log files to an S3 bucket, which you can retain with lifecycle rules and protect with S3 Object Lock.
explanation.concept: Organization trails can capture activity across all accounts.
explanation.examTip: Long-term API audit logs = CloudTrail trail → S3.

stem: A government agency must ensure workloads don't run in AWS Regions outside its country.
prompt: Which control enforces this across all of its AWS accounts?

options.text: Security groups that block foreign IP addresses
options.why: Security groups filter traffic, not which Regions are used.

options.text: A Region policy documented in each team's wiki
options.why: Documentation doesn't enforce anything, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: An SCP denying actions outside approved Regions
options.why: SCPs in AWS Organizations can restrict which Regions accounts can use.

options.text: AWS Budgets alerts in every Region
options.why: Budgets track cost, not Regions, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: A Region-restriction SCP denies requests to unapproved Regions for every account in the OU.
explanation.concept: Control Tower also offers a Region deny control.
explanation.examTip: Restrict Regions for compliance = SCP (or Control Tower Region deny).

stem: An operations team wants a notification when an EC2 instance's CPU stays above 90% for 10 minutes.

options.why: Macie finds sensitive data, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Artifact provides compliance reports, which isn't what this scenario needs.
CloudTrail records API calls, not CPU usage.
CloudWatch collects metrics and can trigger alarms and notifications.

explanation.answer: Amazon CloudWatch alarms watch metrics and take actions, such as sending an Amazon SNS notification, when thresholds are crossed.
explanation.concept: CloudWatch also collects logs and can trigger automated responses.
explanation.examTip: Metrics + alarms = CloudWatch.

stem: A network team wants to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in a VPC.

options.why: Flow Logs capture information about IP traffic in a VPC.
Config records configuration changes, not traffic.
CloudTrail records API calls, not IP traffic on network interfaces.
EC2 metrics show totals like bytes in and out, not per-connection traffic records.

explanation.answer: VPC Flow Logs capture information about accepted and rejected IP traffic and can be sent to CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3.
explanation.concept: Use them to troubleshoot connectivity and as a security data source.
explanation.examTip: Network traffic records in a VPC = VPC Flow Logs.

references.title: Logging IP traffic using VPC Flow Logs

stem: An auditor asks two questions: "What did this security group look like last Tuesday?" and "Who changed it?"

options.text: Trusted Advisor for the first, Inspector for the second
options.why: Neither provides configuration history or API caller identity.

options.text: AWS Config for the first, CloudTrail for the second
options.why: Config keeps configuration history; CloudTrail records the API call and the caller.
Artifact provides AWS compliance reports.
CloudWatch tracks metrics and logs, not configuration history or API identities.

explanation.answer: AWS Config shows what a resource looked like at a point in time. AWS CloudTrail shows who made the API call that changed it.
explanation.concept: The two services are often used together during investigations.
explanation.examTip: What it looked like = Config. Who changed it = CloudTrail.

stem: A financial firm must keep records in Amazon S3 in a way that nobody, including administrators, can delete or overwrite them for five years.

options.why: This is a storage class, not a write-once control.
This speeds up uploads, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

options.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
options.why: Compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting or overwriting objects during the retention period.
Versioning keeps old versions, but versions can still be deleted.

explanation.answer: S3 Object Lock provides write-once-read-many (WORM) protection. In compliance mode, retention can't be shortened or removed by anyone.
explanation.concept: Governance mode allows users with special permissions to override retention.
explanation.examTip: Can't be deleted by anyone for X years = S3 Object Lock compliance mode.

stem: A small company asks whether it must pay to download AWS compliance reports.

options.text: Reports cost a fee per download
options.why: AWS Artifact reports are available at no cost.

options.text: Reports are only for AWS partners
options.why: All customers can use Artifact, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Artifact is available to all customers, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

options.text: AWS Artifact is available at no cost
options.why: Customers can download reports and manage agreements without charge.

explanation.answer: AWS Artifact is a no-cost, self-service portal for AWS compliance reports and agreements.
explanation.concept: Some reports require accepting terms before download.
explanation.examTip: Artifact = free compliance reports.

stem: A security analyst wants to run SQL queries over a year of CloudTrail activity without building a separate data pipeline.

options.why: CloudTrail Lake stores events and lets you query them with SQL.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
The Pricing Calculator estimates costs, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Logs Insights can query logs in CloudWatch Logs, but CloudTrail Lake stores and queries CloudTrail events directly with SQL.

explanation.answer: AWS CloudTrail Lake is a managed data lake for capturing, storing and querying activity events with SQL.
explanation.concept: You can also query CloudTrail logs in S3 using Amazon Athena.
explanation.examTip: Query CloudTrail with SQL directly = CloudTrail Lake.

stem: A compliance officer is listing AWS services that help with audits.
prompt: Which TWO services help a customer show compliance of its own AWS resources? (Select TWO.)

options.why: Audit Manager collects evidence mapped to compliance frameworks.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, not compliance evidence or rule history.
Inspector finds vulnerabilities but isn't a compliance evidence tool for your resources.
CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs but doesn't map evidence to compliance frameworks.
Config evaluates and records resource compliance with rules.

explanation.answer: AWS Config and AWS Audit Manager help customers assess and prove compliance of their own resources. AWS Artifact provides AWS's reports.
explanation.concept: CloudTrail and Security Hub also contribute evidence and checks.
explanation.examTip: Your resources' compliance = Config + Audit Manager (+ CloudTrail, Security Hub).

stem: An auditor wants proof that CloudTrail log files haven't been modified after AWS delivered them.

options.why: Dashboards display metrics, not file integrity.
CloudTrail creates digest files to verify that logs weren't modified, deleted or forged.
Macie finds sensitive data, not log tampering.
This speeds up transfers; it doesn't validate integrity.

explanation.answer: CloudTrail log file integrity validation uses hashing and digital signatures to detect whether log files were changed after delivery.
explanation.concept: Combine with S3 Object Lock and restricted bucket access for strong log protection.
explanation.examTip: Prove logs weren't tampered with = CloudTrail log file integrity validation.

stem: A company serving EU customers asks how AWS supports GDPR.

options.text: GDPR doesn't apply to data processed in the cloud
options.why: GDPR applies regardless of where data is processed.

options.text: AWS makes customers GDPR compliant automatically
options.why: Customers must still meet their own GDPR obligations.

options.text: AWS offers supporting services, a DPA and Region choice
options.why: AWS provides tools and contractual commitments, but the customer remains responsible for its processing.

options.text: AWS stores EU data in the United States by default
options.why: Customers choose Regions; data stays where they put it.

explanation.answer: AWS provides a GDPR-compliant Data Processing Addendum, Region choice and security services; customers remain responsible for how they process personal data.
explanation.concept: This is shared responsibility applied to privacy regulations.
explanation.examTip: AWS supports GDPR; the customer is still responsible for its processing.

stem: A company wants information about AWS compliance programs, such as ISO 27001 and SOC, and how AWS supports customers' compliance.

options.why: Route 53 is DNS, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Marketplace pricing is about third-party software.

options.text: The Amazon EC2 instance types page
options.why: That page lists compute options, which isn't what this scenario needs.
These pages describe the certifications and attestations AWS maintains.

explanation.answer: The AWS Compliance website describes programs AWS participates in, including ISO, SOC, PCI DSS and FedRAMP.
explanation.concept: Download the actual reports from AWS Artifact.
explanation.examTip: Learn about AWS compliance programs = AWS Compliance Programs page; get reports = Artifact.

stem: An application team wants to collect application logs from EC2 instances and Lambda functions in one place and search them.

options.why: CloudWatch Logs collects, stores and searches logs from many sources.
CloudTrail records AWS API calls, not application logs.
Artifact provides compliance reports, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: Amazon CloudWatch Logs centralizes logs from AWS services and applications, with search and metric filters.
explanation.concept: Lambda sends logs to CloudWatch Logs automatically; EC2 uses the CloudWatch agent.
explanation.examTip: Application logs = CloudWatch Logs. AWS API calls = CloudTrail.

stem: A company wants any S3 bucket that becomes public to be fixed automatically.

options.text: Use AWS Artifact to download a weekly bucket exposure report
options.why: Artifact provides AWS compliance reports; it doesn't inspect or fix your buckets.

options.text: Use an AWS Config rule with automatic remediation
options.why: Config rules detect noncompliant buckets and can trigger remediation actions.
This speeds transfers, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Storage class doesn't affect public access.

explanation.answer: AWS Config rules can detect public buckets and use Systems Manager Automation documents to remediate automatically.
explanation.concept: S3 Block Public Access can also prevent public buckets at the account level.
explanation.examTip: Detect + auto-fix configuration drift = Config rules + remediation.

references.title: Remediating noncompliant resources with AWS Config

stem: A company wants to make sure no S3 bucket in its account can ever be made public, even by mistake.

options.why: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Replication copies data; it doesn't block public access.

options.text: S3 Block Public Access at the account level
options.why: Account-level Block Public Access overrides bucket policies and ACLs that would allow public access.
Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage cost.

explanation.answer: S3 Block Public Access settings at the account level prevent any bucket in the account from being made public.
explanation.concept: New buckets have Block Public Access enabled by default.
explanation.examTip: Never public = S3 Block Public Access (account level).

references.title: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage

stem: An operations team wants to know whether an AWS service issue is affecting its specific resources and get notified of scheduled maintenance.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor service limit checks
options.why: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
CloudTrail logs API calls, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Billing alarms track spend, not AWS service events.
It shows events that affect your resources, including scheduled changes.

explanation.answer: The AWS Health Dashboard shows the general status of AWS services and personalized events affecting your account.
explanation.concept: AWS Health events can trigger automated actions through Amazon EventBridge.
explanation.examTip: Is AWS having an issue that affects me? = AWS Health Dashboard.

stem: A company is preparing for an external audit.
prompt: Which TWO tasks can it complete in AWS Artifact? (Select TWO.)

options.why: Artifact Agreements manages agreements like the BAA.
That's AWS Secrets Manager, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
That's AWS Shield, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
That's Amazon Inspector, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Artifact provides AWS compliance reports and certificates.

explanation.answer: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and lets customers review and accept agreements with AWS.
explanation.concept: Artifact doesn't scan, protect or configure your resources.
explanation.examTip: Artifact = reports + agreements. Nothing else.
